WF-03 Step 5 -- close ISS-0106 and carry out the issue-record bookkeeping this run generated. FOUR tasks, all confined to docs/issues/.

**TASK 1 -- close ISS-0106.** Set status: resolved, resolved_in_run: WF03-ISS0106-20260821, resolved_at: <real UTC timestamp from the clock, never from memory>. Then close its GitHub issue. READ ITS github_issue_note FIRST -- there is a trap recorded there: the canonical GitHub issue is #354, but letflow-queue's register_task auto-created a mirror at #355, and #355 is already closed as a duplicate. The note says whoever resolves this must close #354 BY HAND. Close #354 with `gh issue close 354 --comment` citing this run, the local record, and the regression test path.

**TASK 2 -- supersede ISS-0106's stated root cause rather than overwriting it.** Its lines 30-39 assert a ROOT CAUSE (confirmed, not inferred) that this run measured to be WRONG for Symptom 1: the four format failures are not toolchain drift. The pinned Elixir 1.18.3/OTP 27, run in a container against the same tree, rejects the same four files with character-for-character identical diffs -- including the heredoc escape the issue attributes specifically to a formatter version change. Three of the four diffs are ordinary line-length wraps measured at 99-102 characters against a formatter default of 98 that .formatter.exs never overrides, so no Elixir version has ever accepted them. Symptom 2 (the 14 struct-update warnings) IS genuine version-specific behaviour and the original attribution holds for it. Record this the way docs/anti-patterns.md's 'supersede rather than overwrite' guidance requires -- ISS-0063 is the precedent, using a superseded_scoping_note field marked do-not-act-on. The original wrong text must remain readable; a silently corrected record is indistinguishable from one that was right all along, which destroys the audit trail the correction exists to preserve.

**TASK 3 -- addendum to ISS-0046 (already resolved; do NOT reopen it).** Its line 46 records the version attribution for the struct-update warning class as UNCONFIRMED, stating that only 1.20.3 was available to check against and no older Elixir install was reachable. This run settled it: the identical tree compiles with ZERO such warnings under Elixir 1.18.3/OTP 27 in a container, and 14 under 1.20.3/OTP 29. The attribution is CONFIRMED as 1.20-only. Append an addendum saying so, dated, citing this run -- do not edit the original UNCONFIRMED line, append below it.

**TASK 4 -- scope addendum to ISS-0109 (open; do NOT close it).** It records the tenant-schema teardown race but names only Letflow.Definitions.PromotionTest and Letflow.Definitions.PromotionAssertionRerunTest. TEST-RUNNER observed the same symptom this run in Letflow.Definitions.MigrationsTest and Letflow.Engine.PinRebindTest as well, and called it out specifically rather than folding it into the known set. Append a dated addendum widening the observed module set, citing test/reports/report-20260821-WF03-ISS0106-20260821.yaml. Note explicitly that this widens the OBSERVED scope and is not a claim that the root cause changed.

CONTEXT YOU NEED FOR THE CLOSURE COMMENT, because ISS-0106 closes in a state that needs stating precisely rather than as a bare 'fixed'. Both of its symptoms are genuinely fixed and this was verified by the gate itself, not by an agent's say-so: in `mix letflow.check`, step 2 (format --check-formatted) now PASSES and step 3 (compile --warnings-as-errors) now PASSES. But the ALIAS still exits 1, at step 4, for a completely different and already-tracked reason -- ISS-0107 / GH#357, the Windows fake-mix self-recursion, where install_fake_mix/2 joins PATH with a POSIX ':' and writes an extensionless shell script, so on Windows the fake is never resolved and the test shells out to the REAL mix, recursing the suite. TEST-RUNNER confirmed that live by finding three child erl.exe processes running mix test. Say this plainly in both the yaml and the GitHub comment: ISS-0106's two symptoms are fixed, and `mix letflow.check` cannot exit 0 on a Windows host until ISS-0107 is fixed. Do not imply the gate is green, and do not imply ISS-0106 is unfixed.

Do NOT touch the letflow-queue -- ORCH owns all four queue functions and will handle the lock release. Do NOT modify source, tests, or the decision record. Do NOT delete any issue file; these records are append-style audit trail.
acceptance_criteria: ISS-0106 has status: resolved, resolved_in_run and a resolved_at read from the real clock, and its file states precisely that both its symptoms are fixed while mix letflow.check still exits 1 at step 4 due to ISS-0107, without implying either that the gate is green or that ISS-0106 is unfixed
GitHub issue #354 -- the canonical one, not the #355 mirror -- is closed with a comment citing this run, the local record, and the regression test path. State the command and its output

ISS-0106's original root-cause text is PRESERVED verbatim and superseded by a new field rather than edited or deleted; the superseding text states what was measured, distinguishes Symptom 1 (attribution refuted) from Symptom 2 (attribution holds), and is marked do-not-act-on
ISS-0046 carries a dated addendum confirming the 1.20-only attribution its line 46 left UNCONFIRMED, with the original line untouched, and its status is still resolved -- not reopened

ISS-0109 carries a dated addendum widening the observed module set to include Definitions.MigrationsTest and Engine.PinRebindTest, citing the test report, explicitly framed as widening observed scope rather than changing the root cause, and its status is still open -- not closed
No file outside docs/issues/ and your own handoff is modified

result.summary:
All four tasks done; all six acceptance criteria met. Everything below was written into docs/issues/ only, and committed as c085ea2.

===== TASK 1 / AC1 -- ISS-0106 CLOSED, STATE DESCRIBED PRECISELY =====
docs/issues/ISS-0106.yaml now carries status: resolved, resolved_in_run: WF03-ISS0106-20260821, resolved_at: "2026-08-21T03:37:07Z" (read from the clock via `date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"` at the start of this step, not from memory; it precedes this handoff's own completed_at). A new `resolution` field states the closure condition in both directions, deliberately refusing to round either way: (i) BOTH symptoms are fixed and this was verified by the gate itself, not by an agent's claim -- in `mix letflow.check` at commit ec32dcd (run 2026-08-21T03:19 UTC, recorded under `letflow_check:` in test/reports/report-20260821-WF03-ISS0106-20260821.yaml), step 2 `format --check-formatted` PASSES and step 3 `compile --warnings-as-errors` PASSES; (ii) the ALIAS still exits 1, at STEP 4 (`letflow.check.test`), for a completely different and separately tracked reason -- ISS-0107 / GH#357, the Windows fake-mix self-recursion, where install_fake_mix/2 joins PATH with a POSIX ':' and writes an extensionless shell script, so on Windows the fake is never resolved and the test shells out to the real mix, recursing the suite (TEST-RUNNER confirmed it live by finding three child erl.exe processes running `mix test`). The field says in as many words that the gate is NOT green, that ISS-0106 is NOT the reason it is not green, and that `mix letflow.check` cannot exit 0 on a Windows host until ISS-0107 is fixed. It also records what shipped (Part A 9ca2071 pin move + `mix letflow.check_toolchain` drift check; Part B 3307c22 reformat; Part C 7d7ad9f struct-update annotations; REVIEWER's decision-0005 sign-off 1a505a1) and the regression path.

===== TASK 1 / AC2 -- GH#354 CLOSED (NOT THE #355 MIRROR) =====
Read ISS-0106's `github_issue_note` FIRST, as instructed; it is the reason #354 was targeted. #355 was letflow-queue's register_task auto-mirror and was already closed as a duplicate, so a release_lock(status: "done") on task 170 would have closed #355 and left the canonical issue open.
Command: `gh issue close 354 --comment "<multi-paragraph comment>"`.
Output, verbatim: `✓ Closed issue tvolodi/letflow#354 (ISS-0106: main fails mix format --check-formatted and --warnings-as-errors under Elixir 1.20/OTP 29 (toolchain drift from .tool-versions pin))`, exit 0.
Verified rather than assumed, `gh issue view 354 --json number,state,closedAt` -> {"closedAt":"2026-08-21T03:39:08Z","number":354,"state":"CLOSED"}. (Pre-close, the same query returned state OPEN, so the close is this step's effect and not a pre-existing state.)
The comment cites: this run (WF03-ISS0106-20260821, branch feature/WF03-ISS0106-20260821); the local record (docs/issues/ISS-0106.yaml with its new status/resolved_in_run/resolved_at); the regression test path (test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_toolchain_test.exs, 30 tests, with the fail-then-pass and mutant evidence); the same two-sided gate statement as the yaml (steps 2 and 3 pass, step 4 still red for ISS-0107/#357); the root-cause correction; and a closing note that #354 is canonical and #355 the already-closed mirror.

===== TASK 2 / AC3 -- ROOT CAUSE SUPERSEDED, NOT OVERWRITTEN =====
The `description` field is byte-for-byte untouched -- `git diff --numstat docs/issues/ISS-0106.yaml` is `84 1`, and the single deleted line is `status: open`, replaced by `status: resolved`. The original "ROOT CAUSE (confirmed, not inferred)" block (filed lines 30-39) and its "Proposed resolution" paragraph are fully readable exactly as filed.
Two new fields do the superseding, following ISS-0063's `superseded_scoping_note` precedent as instructed:
  * `superseded_root_cause_note` -- marks the original SUPERSEDED with a timestamp, says "Do NOT act on it" explicitly, names option (a) of the Proposed-resolution paragraph as the specific thing not to act on (that check WAS run and is refuted), and states the reason the original is retained rather than corrected in place: a silently corrected record is indistinguishable from one that was right all along, which destroys the audit trail the correction exists to preserve.
  * `corrected_root_cause` -- what was MEASURED, in a throwaway elixir:1.18.3-otp-27 container against the same tree, and it distinguishes the two symptoms rather than blanket-refuting the issue. SYMPTOM 1: ATTRIBUTION REFUTED -- the pinned 1.18.3/OTP 27 formatter rejects the SAME four files with character-for-character identical diffs, INCLUDING the `\"""` heredoc escape in variable_merge.ex that the original attributes specifically to a formatter version change; three of the four diffs are ordinary line-length wraps measured at 99-102 chars against a formatter default of 98 that .formatter.exs never overrides, so no Elixir version has ever accepted them; installing the pinned toolchain would have left the format check failing on exactly the same four files. SYMPTOM 2: ATTRIBUTION HOLDS -- genuine version-specific behaviour, zero such warnings under 1.18.3/OTP 27 and 14 under 1.20.3/OTP 29 on the identical tree, and the original text is correct about it. Concluding line states the consequence: ISS-0106 as filed bundles two defects with different root causes under one failing command, and only Symptom 2 was toolchain drift.

===== TASK 3 / AC4 -- ISS-0046 ADDENDUM =====
Appended `version_attribution_addendum` (dated 2026-08-21T03:37:07Z, citing run WF03-ISS0106-20260821). `git diff --numstat docs/issues/ISS-0046.yaml` is `44 0` -- pure addition, zero deletions, so the UNCONFIRMED paragraph in `description` is untouched and stands as the record of what was knowable on 2026-08-18. `status:` is still `resolved`; ISS-0046 is NOT reopened, and the addendum says so in its own text so a future reader cannot mistake it for a reopening. Content: CONFIRMED 1.20-only -- an older Elixir became reachable not as a host install but as a pinned container, and on one identical tree 1.18.3/OTP 27 gives `mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors` exit 0 with `grep -c 'is expected on struct update'` = 0 and no `warning:` line at all, while 1.20.3/OTP 29 gives exit 1 with 14, all of this class. Records the mechanism (1.20's set-theoretic checker re-infers a private function's parameter types across an unspec'd boundary instead of inheriting the caller's narrowed type; 1.18.3's does not perform that analysis), and the corollary that makes ISS-0046's own shipped fix safe under either toolchain: the explicit `%Struct{} = var` pattern-match idiom is ordinary Elixir in both versions -- the patched file compiles warning-free AND format-clean under 1.18.3 -- so it is better-typed source, not a version workaround. Also notes that the ISS-0044 discrepancy ISS-0046 flagged rather than explained away is CONSISTENT with the toolchain explanation now that the version difference is measured, while explicitly not claiming which of the two candidate explanations applied to ISS-0044 itself.

===== TASK 4 / AC5 -- ISS-0109 ADDENDUM =====
Appended `observed_scope_addendum` (dated 2026-08-21T03:37:07Z). `git diff --numstat docs/issues/ISS-0109.yaml` is `49 0` -- pure addition. `status:` is still `open`; ISS-0109 is NOT closed, and the addendum states that in its first paragraph. Its second paragraph is the framing the AC requires, stated before any of the new data so it cannot be skimmed past: this widens the OBSERVED module set ONLY, it is not a claim that the root cause changed, both candidate mechanisms in the existing `mechanism:` field are still live and still need a real diagnosis run, and it must not be read as progress on root cause. New modules: Letflow.Definitions.MigrationsTest (test/letflow/definitions/migrations_test.exs:662) and Letflow.Engine.PinRebindTest (test/letflow/engine/pin_rebind_test.exs:351), both 3F000 invalid_schema_name inside TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/1 on a schema the test itself had just provisioned -- the same shape as this issue's failure 3. Cites test/reports/report-20260821-WF03-ISS0106-20260821.yaml and names the four sections of it that carry the evidence (`load_dependence`, `the_pin_rebind_failure_deserved_extra_scrutiny_and_got_it`, `newly_uncovered_failures`, and the MINOR entry in `findings_for_orch`). Carries the corroborating circumstance, which is itself evidence for the already-recorded full-suite-only character: two full runs of the SAME commit ec32dcd ten minutes apart, same host and database, no code change, produced 13 and 15 failures, and these two modules are exactly the delta -- failing only in the more contended run 2, a child process of the gate whose own Check.TestTest spawned three further nested suites against the same Postgres. Also carries TEST-RUNNER's PinRebindTest scrutiny (that file IS in this branch's diff, so "not in the diff" was unavailable as an argument and was not used: the only hunk re-wraps a list literal at lines 513-517, whitespace only with the token stream unchanged, while the failure is at line 351 in provisioned_tenant/0 several hundred lines away, and re-wrapping a list literal cannot drop a Postgres schema). Records why this is an addendum rather than a new id: the class already has this open record, and a fourth id for the same race would repeat the ISS-numbering collision class docs/anti-patterns.md warns about -- which this very file's own renumber_note is an instance of.

===== AC6 -- SCOPE DISCIPLINE =====
Exactly four files written by me: the three under docs/issues/ and this handoff. `git status --short` before commit showed only ' M docs/issues/ISS-0046.yaml', ' M docs/issues/ISS-0106.yaml', ' M docs/issues/ISS-0109.yaml' as my modifications. Untouched, as instructed: docs/anti-patterns.md and docs/status/requirement_status.yaml (DOC-UPDATER is on those concurrently for this same run); handoffs/registry.json and handoffs/orchestrator.log (ORCH's -- both still showing their pre-existing ' M' from before this step, per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md §4 and §7); the untracked docs/issues/ISS-0110.yaml (ORCH's, left exactly as found); and all source, tests, and docs/migration/decisions/0005-pin-formatting-toolchain.md. No issue file was deleted -- these records are append-style audit trail. letflow-queue was NOT called: none of its four functions was invoked, and the task-170 lock release is ORCH's.
All three edited files were re-parsed with `yaml.safe_load` after editing rather than assumed well-formed: all three load, and the parse confirms ISS-0106 status=resolved, ISS-0046 status=resolved, ISS-0109 status=open.

issues.description: The ISS-0106 / #354-vs-#355 trap is now the SECOND recorded instance of the same defect, not a one-off: ISS-0109's own github_issue_note documents the identical shape for task 172 (#358 canonical, #359 auto-mirror closed as duplicate, and a future release_lock(status: "done") will close the wrong one). letflow-queue's register_task auto-creates a mirror GitHub issue even when the caller already filed one, and release_lock closes the MIRROR. Both times the mitigation has been a hand-written warning in a yaml field plus a human-equivalent agent remembering to read it. That mitigation worked here only because this handoff called it out explicitly. Worth fixing at the source in letflow-queue (either have register_task accept and adopt an existing issue url instead of minting a mirror, or have release_lock close the issue recorded on the task rather than the one it created) rather than adding a third note. Out of scope for this step, which is confined to docs/issues/.

ISS-0107 (the Windows fake-mix self-recursion, GH#357) is now the sole reason `mix letflow.check` cannot exit 0 on a Windows host, and this run has shown it is self-sustaining -- the gate runs `mix test`, whose Check.TestTest spawns `mix test` again. With ISS-0106's two symptoms now green, every remaining red in that alias is ISS-0107's, which makes it the standing-red-gate risk ISS-0106 itself warned about ('learning to treat a red gate as normal') inherited by a new owner. Flagged for ORCH's queue prioritisation; nothing about it was changed by this step.
